name: Vienna & Eastern Austria
why_kept_merged: Matches the real NUTS-1 Ostösterreich macro-region (Vienna + Lower Austria + Burgenland) exactly, and Vienna's metropolitan commuter/economic gravity already spans all three Länder in practice; splitting the cultural unit along Land lines would cut through one functioning catchment area rather than honor a real internal boundary.

name: Basel
why_kept_merged: Mirrors the official Swiss Grossregion Nordwestschweiz exactly (Basel-Stadt + Basel-Landschaft + Aargau) — Switzerland's own statistical/economic macro-region convention already treats these three cantons as one functional unit around Basel's urban core.

name: Bern-Mittelland
parliaments_inside: Parlement de la République et Canton du Jura
why_kept_merged: Mirrors the official Swiss Grossregion Espace Mittelland exactly (Bern + Fribourg + Solothurn + Neuchâtel + Jura); no single one of the five cantons clears a standalone-catchment threshold on its own, and Bern's federal-capital gravity already organizes the cluster.

name: Romandie / Geneva-Lausanne
why_kept_merged: Mirrors the official Swiss Grossregion Région lémanique exactly (Genève + Vaud + Valais); the three cantons share the Lac Léman/Rhône-valley catchment and Francophone identity that the cultural-unit layer is organized around.

name: Central & Eastern Switzerland
why_kept_merged: Approximates the official Swiss Grossregionen Zentralschweiz + Ostschweiz combined, per the v0.1.0 zone-1 spec's broad-combination call; the widest single exception in the dataset, flagged there as a future-subdivision candidate. Schaffhausen (v0.1.2) is the first canton split back out of it, for its distinct 1501 founding-era history — the remaining eleven still read as one cultural-unit atom even though each canton keeps its own parliament.

name: Upper Silesia (Katowice)
why_kept_merged: Śląskie and Opolskie voivodeships both sit inside the historic, dialectally-continuous Upper Silesian identity zone (Ślązacy self-declaration, shared Silesian ethnolect); splitting on the voivodeship-sejmik line would cut through one linguistic-cultural continuum for a purely statistical boundary.

name: Wielkopolska & Western Poland (Poznań)
why_kept_merged: Poznań's historic Wielkopolska core organizes the wider western-Poland catchment; none of Zachodniopomorskie or Lubuskie alone clears a distinct urban-hub identity strong enough to justify a separate cultural unit from Poznań's gravity.

name: Pomerania, Kuyavia & Warmia-Masuria (Gdańsk)
why_kept_merged: Matches Statistics Poland's own PL6 macroregion exactly; kept as the default cultural unit's broad view, but the strength of this merge is honestly graded (strong for Kashubia, weak for Kuyavia, weakest for Warmia-Masuria per the user-supplied fit table) — see the variant-set section below for the split view that exposes this gradient directly.

name: Eastern Poland (Lublin-Rzeszów-Białystok)
why_kept_merged: Mirrors the EU's own 'Polska Wschodnia' (Eastern Poland) cohesion-policy macroregion precedent exactly; none of the four voivodeships has a dominant single urban hub on the scale of Poznań, Wrocław or Kraków, so they are kept as one polycentric catch-all rather than four thin, hub-less units.

name: Bohemia (Prague)
why_kept_merged: Bohemia's own identity (Čechy) sits a full level above the kraj (region council) tier introduced in 2000 for administrative decentralization, not to express cultural boundaries; kraj lines routinely bisect functionally and dialectally continuous Bohemian territory.

name: Moravia (Brno)
why_kept_merged: Matches the Czech usage 'Morava a Slezsko' convention that already pairs Czech Silesia with the Moravian kraje in everyday and administrative language; Moravian self-identification (2011 census 'Moravian nationality' entries) runs across all four kraje as one continuum, not four separate ones.

name: Bratislava & Western Slovakia
why_kept_merged: Amendment A1.8 supersedes an earlier finer split: Slovakia is authored as exactly two units (capital-region west, Košice-Prešov east), so the capital region's own catchment necessarily absorbs six kraj-level self-governing regions; the reasoning is the strength of Bratislava's west-Slovak gravity, not a claim that the six kraje lack real assemblies.

name: Eastern Slovakia (Košice-Prešov)
why_kept_merged: Amendment A1.8: Košice and Prešov are kept as one dipole cultural unit on the strength of their shared Rusyn/Ukrainian-minority basis and joint distinctness from the Bratislava-oriented west, even though each kraj retains its own samosprávny kraj assembly.
